newsitem.title: USA: Inland says spinoff proposal rejected.
newsitem.headline: Inland says spinoff proposal rejected.

text.p: Inland Steel Industries Inc said a proposal to spin off the company's remaining 87 percent stake in Ryerson Tull Inc was rejected by shareholders Wednesday at the annual meeting here.
The proposal was sponsored by Greenway Partners L.P. which owns a stake in Inland, the sixth largest U.S. steel maker.

At the meeting, Inland said 17.3 percent of the voting power of all voting securities outstanding and represented at the meeting voted in favor of the Greenway proposal. The proposal was opposed by Inland directors and management.

"Clearly, the overwhelming majority of Inland's shareholders agree that the board is in the best position to determine the appropriateness and timing of strategic alternatives," said chief executive Robert Darnall.
Alfred Kingsley, principal of Greenway, said the group is a long-term investor and will monitor its Inland holdings.
"We'll see how the company does," Kingsley said.
Besides proposing a spin-off or a letter-stock issuance of Inland's remaining Ryerson stake, Kingsley said Greenway also proposed that Inland seek a merger partner.

"We think that there should be some consolidation in the industry now. Don't wait for a downturn when everybody's looking around and they think they're going bust. Do it when things are good and then maybe things will get better. So that's our thought," Kingsley said.

In a press conference following the meeting, Darnall reiterated that he is open to change at Inland. "I'm willing to consider options that create a stronger steel company," he said in answer to a question about possible mergers.
He declined to comment on whether any other talks have followed those that occurred last year between Inland and USX-US Steel Group, the largest U.S. steelmaker.
Those talks were halted late last year after Inland decided against combining the two companies.
"There's an intellectual case that can be made for industry consolidation, but nothing has happened," Darnall said.
